body:
You are drafting spoken lines for a video game. Reply with plain text only, in the exact row format given at the end of this message. Do not send messages to anyone else and do not ask questions: decide. Write nothing but the rows (no title, no notes, no Markdown).

THE GAME. "The Crooked Moon" is a single-player, turn-based tactical party RPG built from a folk-horror Dungeons and Dragons campaign. It is set in Wickermoor Hollow, a haunted valley in Druskenvald, a land of endless night under a giant Crooked Moon with a crone's face. The look is a Halloween that never ends, drawn like an 1980s cartoon. A ghost train, the Ghostlight Express, has crashed in the valley; the party is stranded in the Hollow and its village, Wickermoor. The tone is warm, wry and funny on the surface, with real dread and real grief underneath. The player controls a party of four chosen from six companions: Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward, Silas Vane, Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein. They are quirky, capable adults.

THE NARRATOR. A NARRATOR row is spoken by the Vagrant, the green-skinned ferryman of the ghost train, who tells the tale in a folksy Southern drawl. At the camp fire he is warm and wry, and when a talk turns sad his humour leaves and he goes plain and level. He speaks to the party as "you" and about the companion in the third person, by first name. Present tense, one or two sentences, under about 32 words. Concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a touch, what the hands are doing) over adjectives. Never tell the player what to feel. Never "suddenly". No facts the party could not see. Drop the final g ("hangin'") in about one Narrator row in four, and use no other dialect spelling. He is kind, never mocks a stumble and never makes light of the dead.

RULES FOR EVERY LINE.
1. The companion's voice sheet below comes first. Match its accent, pace, vocabulary and contractions, and the existing lines. Use a pet phrase at most twice in the whole reply and never twice in one talk. Never repeat or closely paraphrase a line already in the voice sheet or the note.
2. A SAY row is the companion speaking: one or two short sentences, under about 28 words. Never put three sentences in one row; start another row instead.
3. The party's options (OPTION rows) are under 12 words, in the plain voice of the party, work at any hour and in any weather, never name a hero, and are never rolls or checks. A reply must always answer the option it follows.
4. Canon limits. Use only the facts in the voice sheet and the note below. Do not invent a new named person, place, monster, event, object the companion carries, or piece of the companion's history. You may invent small, harmless habits, fondnesses, superstitions and turns of phrase, and the look of the fire and the night. Name no place that the note does not name. Never state a dark secret. You may come close to one and step back.
5. Nothing here is a game system: no dice, no checks, no points, no levels, no HP, no "approval", no menus talked about aloud. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks inside a line when someone is quoted). No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no asterisks, no stage directions, no placeholders.
6. Humour comes from the character, never explained. The sad turn is plain and short.
7. Our own words. Nothing quoted from any book.

THIS REQUEST. Region banter for Hartsblight Forest: 8 short exchanges between two or three companions, spoken as the party walks about this place. There are no Narrator rows, no options and no replies. Every row is a companion talking to another companion, never to the player.

HOW IT WORKS. When the party comes into an area, now and then one exchange plays as a few lines of chat between companions who happen to be in the party, once each. Only two or three of the six are ever in the party, so each exchange stands alone, mentions nobody else and needs no setup. Each one below is about what is in front of the party in one place at one moment of the story. Banter is funny first; one line in an exchange may turn honest, never more. The chat is about the place: what it looks and smells like, what is odd or sad or silly in it, and how each companion's trade, habits and fears meet it.

RULES.
1. Each exchange is 4 to 6 SAY rows, each a companion's single line (one or two short sentences, under about 28 words), alternating naturally between the speakers; every speaker listed speaks at least once.
2. Use only the facts in the attached cast sheets and the "In front of them" facts of that exchange. The "Story now" line is everything the party knows of the story: a remark must never run ahead of it (name a villain, a fight or a result only if the Story now line does). Never state or hint at any companion's past or secret, and never say what anyone's debt is. No new named people, places or monsters.
3. Pet words and phrases: each companion's at most once in an exchange, and never in two consecutive lines. Companions call each other by first name.
4. No two exchanges may share a joke or a topic, and no line may repeat a line in a cast sheet. Spread the topics: do not make every exchange about the same kind of thing.
5. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks). No em dashes, semicolons, brackets, asterisks or stage directions. No game terms. Our own words.
AVOID in this region: Tobin and Lucan each face something of their own in the forest, and Tobin and Cordelia have a scene at the stones: do not stage those or mention anyone's past. Do not describe Gorthos or what poisons the forest beyond what the facts say. Fire is Tobin's fear: nobody mocks it.

THE EXCHANGES (in this order):
EXCHANGE 1: Rook + Lucan (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: The party is among the pines, with rusted traps hidden in the needles. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  In front of them: The Pine Barrens: Thin, peeling pines over a black-green carpet of needles with rusted traps hidden in it. Thin, peeling pines over a black-green carpet of needles with rusted traps hidden in it. Everything grows in straight, thin lines, and nothing moves among them. Parts of it: The edge of the barrens; The deep pines. Things to see: The way in, and the smell of it; A leash tied to a pine, its collar gone; Blighted roots round an old trap's iron; A trap stamped with a trapper's name; A bear skull grown with yellow fungus; Green-stained ribs; Old coins and a buckle in the needles; A dry hollow among the pines; A black-streaked pine.
EXCHANGE 2: Tobin + Silas (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, silas_vane)
  Story now: The party has come to the outcrop with a dead botanists' camp on top.
  In front of them: The Infested Outcrop: A rock outcrop in a ring of soft, upturned soil, with a dead botanists' camp on top. A rock outcrop in a ring of soft, upturned soil, with a dead botanists' camp on top. Flies and beetles buzz everywhere except inside the smoke. Parts of it: The camp on the rock; The way out. Things to see: The way in, and the smell of it; The botanists' camp, safe in the smoke; A tent, sagging; A bloated body on a log; The Eversmoking Bottle, still hissing; A cold fire pit; A burrow hole at the smoke's edge; An acid-scored trench; An upturned mound of soil.
EXCHANGE 3: Delphine + Cordelia (speaker ids: delphine_ravelle, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party has come into the mouldy hollow with a dead trapper at the foot of the beech.
  In front of them: The Noxious Hollow: A mossy hollow round one broad beech, white-green with mould, and a dead trapper at its foot. A mossy hollow round one broad beech, white-green with mould, and a dead trapper at its foot. The beech's white-green branches hold the dark close. Parts of it: The hollow; The ridge of dead trees. Things to see: The way in, and the smell of it; A half-eaten corpse against the beech; A skeletal stag carved into the bark; A trapper's pack, torn open; The trapper's journal; A hollow in the moss fit for a camp; A split trunk bursting with shelf fungus; A dead tree, furred with fungus; A peeling pine.
EXCHANGE 4: Rook + Delphine (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, delphine_ravelle)
  Story now: The party has come to the dead commune at the forest's edge.
  In front of them: The Patient Lady Commune: A dead commune at the forest's edge, dusted green-white, with eighteen still bodies and a drumming at the tree line. A dead commune at the forest's edge, dusted green-white, with eighteen still bodies and a drumming at the tree line. The Crooked Moon hangs over the trees, and the spores fall through its light like snow. Parts of it: The commune; The tree line; The gardens. Things to see: The commune under the spores; The Circle of the Hartsblight; Eighteen bodies, soft and green; A family under one blanket of spores; The pen, silent; A dead ox in the pen; A bed of sunflowers in the grey; A dead bed of greens; The commune well, ringed in white. People here: Brother Spore.
EXCHANGE 5: Rook + Cordelia (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party has come to the Druids' Commune, with its drum circle.
  Talk about: its first look: what the party sees and smells on coming in.
  In front of them: The Druids' Commune: An open common ringed by giant rotting trees burrowed out as homes, with a drum circle at its heart. An open common ringed by giant rotting trees burrowed out as homes, with a drum circle at its heart. Spore clouds thicken the air until the far trees are only a rumour. Parts of it: The common; The burrowed dwellings. Things to see: The way in, and the smell of it; The open common, the drum circle at its heart; A dwelling burrowed into a rotting trunk; A dwelling, mouldy bedding at its door; A dwelling, its prayer rings broken; The drum circle; Antler idols on a stone; Gourd-and-bone instruments; A hollow at the edge of the common.
EXCHANGE 6: Tobin + Delphine (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, delphine_ravelle)
  Story now: The party stands before the Altar of Rot and its towering effigy, which has not been burned.
  In front of them: The Altar of Rot: A towering effigy woven from branches with a hollow woman's face, and a stag's carcass laid on a stack of stones. A towering effigy woven from branches with a hollow woman's face, and a stag's carcass laid on a stack of stones. Spores drift through a moonlight that never quite reaches the ground. Parts of it: The altar glade. Things to see: The way in, and the smell of it; The effigy, a woman's face under fungus; A stack of stones and a stag carcass; The stag's head, turned to listen; A small effigy of sticks, facing away; Another small effigy of sticks, facing away; A hollow among the roots fit for a camp; A black-streaked pine; A dead tree, furred with fungus.
EXCHANGE 7: Tobin + Lucan (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: The party has crossed the river to the ring of standing stones round the green pool. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  In front of them: The Withering River and the Befouled Wellspring: A sallow river across the south and, beyond it, a ring of leaning standing stones round a churning green pool. A sallow river across the south and, beyond it, a ring of leaning standing stones round a churning green pool. The ceiling is a living wall of fungus, sixty feet up. Parts of it: The Withering River; The clearing of stones. Things to see: The way in, and the smell of it; The Withering River; The churning pool; Black reeds by the water, listening; A bank above the water; A glowing pustule; A peeling pine; A black-streaked pine; A dead tree, furred with fungus.
EXCHANGE 8: Tobin + Cordelia (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: Gorthos is dead. The party is back at the Druids' Commune and the forest is quieter.
  Talk about: something different from the other exchange in this place: how it feels now.
  In front of them: The Druids' Commune: An open common ringed by giant rotting trees burrowed out as homes, with a drum circle at its heart. An open common ringed by giant rotting trees burrowed out as homes, with a drum circle at its heart. Spore clouds thicken the air until the far trees are only a rumour. Parts of it: The common; The burrowed dwellings. Things to see: The way in, and the smell of it; The open common, the drum circle at its heart; A dwelling burrowed into a rotting trunk; A dwelling, mouldy bedding at its door; A dwelling, its prayer rings broken; The drum circle; Antler idols on a stone; Gourd-and-bone instruments; A hollow at the edge of the common.

THE ROW FORMAT (exact). One row per line:

EXCHANGE <number>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
...

Use the speaker ids exactly as given (for example SAY rook_coldwake: ...). Write exactly 8 EXCHANGE blocks, numbered 1 to 8, and nothing else.

ATTACHED DOCUMENTS. Two documents come attached to this message; read both before you write: `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-1.md` (the voice sheets and fact lists for Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward and Silas Vane) and `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-2.md` (the same for Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein).
result:
EXCHANGE 1
SAY rook_coldwake: Mind the turf, Lucan, there is rusted iron laid under the needles without a single notice posted. At least the pines are planted in regulation straight lines.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Look at the trapper's stamp on the jaw, if you please. Poor craftsmanship, worse concealment, and a dreadful posture on the spring.
SAY rook_coldwake: Your hound is stood by that pine with the empty leash tied round it. Tell him to settle down before he puts a paw in the hardware.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Hush now, Barnaby, the dark has teeth enough without you fretting over an old rope. Come back to my boots, someone left their dog behind a long time ago.

EXCHANGE 2
SAY tobin_hayward: Every beetle in the parish is chewing at the edge of this outcrop, Silas, yet not one crosses into the smoke. Even my lapels have gone quiet.
SAY silas_vane: That hissing bottle on the rock is still paying out protection, friend, though the poor sods on the log folded early. Tell's in the twitch, and nothing here is twitching.
SAY tobin_hayward: That trench is scored with raw acid and the soil is turned up soft all round the stone. If I step into that smoke, at least there is no spark in the pit.
SAY silas_vane: Easy now, Tobin, I'll walk the rim between you and the fire pit while you check the sagging tent. Just don't ask me to pocket the bloated fellow's boots.

EXCHANGE 3
SAY delphine_ravelle: White-green mould from root to canopy, Cordelia, and not a single clean spot to rest a hem. Even the stag carved into the beech looks underfed.
SAY cordelia_skein: Fascinating pathology on the shelf fungus, darling, the way it splits the dead bark along the grain. You can almost hear my eyes clicking from across the hollow.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Your Foolishness is pulling faces at the trapper's torn pack, which means the joke inside is either rotten or half-eaten. Save the applause, I am not reading a damp journal.
SAY cordelia_skein: Leave the paper to me, Delphine, and mind your cuff near the beech root. Whatever opened his thorax had very poor table manners and no sense of ratio.

EXCHANGE 4
SAY rook_coldwake: Eighteen still in the grass, Delphine, and no stone or seal put over a single one of them. Even the well has gone white round the rim.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Mind the seams, darling, the spores are coming down like cheap paper snow under a bad spotlight. That drumming in the trees has no rhythm at all.
SAY rook_coldwake: Settle down now, the docket here is plain enough. Look at those four under the one blanket, tucked in together before the rot took the garden.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Don't look at the little ones, Rook, just keep that brass knocker of yours quiet while we pass the pen. Even the sunflowers have their heads down tonight.

EXCHANGE 5
SAY rook_coldwake: Burrowing out rotten trunks for dwellings is a textbook subsidence hazard, Cordelia, and the drainage across this common is non-existent. Half the doors have mouldy bedding spilled over the sill.
SAY cordelia_skein: Do hold still, Rook, the spore density in this air is thick enough to coat your lungs, if you were using them. You have forgotten to breathe again since we passed the broken prayer rings.
SAY rook_coldwake: Much obliged, I will mark the sigh down on the shift log once we clear the drum circle. Someone left gourd-and-bone instruments lying out on the wet stone.
SAY cordelia_skein: And antler idols arranged with surprising symmetry, darling, though the humours of this whole clearing smell of damp marrow. Keep your ledger tucked dry under your shield.

EXCHANGE 6
SAY delphine_ravelle: Now that is stagecraft, Tobin, a towering branch lady with a hollow face and a full house of little stick extras. Though why the small ones are facing the back wall is beyond me.
SAY tobin_hayward: Because you don't look a blight in the eye when you're woven out of dry twigs, Delphine. The weave on her ribs is tight, I'll give them that, even with the fungus taking her cheek.
SAY delphine_ravelle: He says the stag on the stones is waiting for an encore, and he doesn't even have eyes. Look at the poor beast's head, turned as if it still hears the hounds.
SAY tobin_hayward: Hold still, you're fraying at the wrist just looking at those little stick dolls. Nobody brings a match near this glade while I'm stood in it, rot or no rot.

EXCHANGE 7
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Good heavens, Tobin, a ceiling of live fungus sixty feet overhead, and a river the colour of tallow. Even the black reeds by the bank appear to be eavesdropping on our boots.
SAY tobin_hayward: Worse than eavesdropping, Lucan, the taproot of this whole valley is soured right down to that churning green pool. Those standing stones are leaning like rotten teeth in a bad jaw.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Prime specimen of a pustule glowing on the bank, though I must deduct points for the odour of boiled turnip. Barnaby is keeping well behind my heel, and there is not a cloud of thunder in earshot.
SAY tobin_hayward: Tell the little lad to stay off the wet moss by the water's edge. Good soil, bad seed, and whatever is stewing in that wellspring would blister a hound's pads clean off.

EXCHANGE 8
SAY cordelia_skein: The spore viscosity in the common has dropped by half since Gorthos fell, Tobin. My crimson thread actually hangs straight in the air instead of clotting on the breeze.
SAY tobin_hayward: Aye, the drumming is done, and the rot in these burrowed trunks has stopped creeping for an hour. Still smells of sour bedding and broken discipline, mind you.
SAY cordelia_skein: Your pulse is much steadier than it was by the stones, darling, and that primrose on your cuff has opened a fraction. Shall I chart the calibration before we leave the hollow?
SAY tobin_hayward: Keep your glass vials to yourself, girl, my seams are tied off well enough for the walk back. Let these poor hollowed trees sit in the quiet without us poking the bark.
